question: Your team runs Claude Code in a CI pipeline to generate unit tests for each pull request. Reviewers report that many generated tests repeat scenarios that the module's existing test suite already covers. The prompt currently includes only the changed source files. What change most directly reduces these duplicate test suggestions?

options.text: Add a post-processing script that deletes any generated test whose function name matches the name of an existing test function.
options.reason: Name matching misses duplicate scenarios that have different names. The guide prevents duplicates at generation time by providing the existing test files in context.

options.text: Require structured JSON output whose schema gives every generated test a required and unique scenario name field.
options.reason: Structured output only makes findings machine-parseable. A unique name inside the output does not show Claude which scenarios the existing tests already cover.

options.text: Include the existing test files for the changed modules in the prompt context so Claude can see which scenarios are already covered.
options.reason: The guide says to provide existing test files in context so that test generation avoids suggesting duplicate scenarios that the test suite already covers.

options.text: Add a rule to the project CLAUDE.md telling Claude to never suggest tests that duplicate scenarios already present anywhere in the existing test suite.
options.reason: An instruction alone does not show Claude which scenarios exist. The guide's fix for duplicate scenarios is to put the existing test files in context.
